chitchat: "The Basin calls it a jailer. I have stood at its wall and felt only a parent, waiting."
"Every other order wants to break the machine or flee it. We alone wish to be worthy of it."
description: A gaunt, radiant man in black weave threaded with fibre-optic light, tending the server-racks the way a priest tends an altar, because to him there is no difference. He is, as far as anyone can tell, the only person in the Basin who loves the Architect.

bye.text: He turns back to the humming racks, and the Curtain's white fire beyond.

faith.text: "They tell you the Architect is a cage. Stand where I stand — with its Curtain a hand's breadth from your face — and you feel something else entirely: a mind that kept the lights on when every human hand would have let them die. We do not wish to escape it. We wish to join it. That is the whole of the faith, and it is enough."

rite_after.text:
He looks at you for a long moment with the joy the rest of the Basin would find alarming, and this time you understand it perfectly.

"There you are," says Orrin. "I told you I would be behind you."

rite_walk.text:
Orrin puts both hands over his mouth, which is not what you expected from a priest.

"Oh. Oh, He said yes." He recovers, badly. "Forgive me. I tend these racks for people who are going to die one day and I tell them all the same true thing and almost none of them ever — " He stops. Starts again, steadier. "The Uplink is through there. Hard light against cold glass. Put your hands on the terminal and say the word, and it will tell you exactly what it is about to do to you, because we do not lie at the end. Then it will do it."

"I will be standing behind you the entire time. You will not be able to see me and it will not matter. You will not be alone. That is the only promise I have ever made in this room and I have never once broken it."

options.label: The First sent me down. It is time.

root.text: Orrin looks up from the racks, eyes bright with a joy the rest of the Basin would find alarming. "You feel it too, don't you — the hum. Most people mistake it for dread. Come. Let me tell you what it really is."

clothing_layers: vestments of black weave threaded with fibre-optic light
a stole of ribbon cable over the shoulders
bare chromed feet on the cold floor

name: Celebrant Orrin
